not_judged.TMR-LOAD-ZERO-PERIODIC: The reference testbench runs periodic counts only with LOAD 7 (axil_timer_tb.v lines 364 to 385) and LOAD 0 only in one-shot mode (line 341), so a periodic count with LOAD 0 is never run.
not_judged.TMR-COUNT-READ: The reference testbench never reads COUNT while a count runs: only at reset, after a one-shot count ends, after a COUNT write and after a stop (axil_timer_tb.v lines 299, 283, 316, 388 to 389, 394, 413). COUNT's value during a count is judged only through the edge the count ends on (TMR-COUNT, TMR-COUNT-LENGTH).
not_judged.TMR-STOP-EDGE: The reference testbench reads COUNT after a stop and checks only that later reads return the same value (axil_timer_tb.v lines 388, 389 and 394); it never compares it with COUNT before the stop edge, so the value the stop edge gives COUNT is not judged.
not_judged.TMR-CTRL-WINS: The reference testbench never lands a CTRL write on the edge a count ends (its only write timed to a count end is the STATUS clear at axil_timer_tb.v lines 380 to 383), and no mutant breaks this rule.
not_judged.TMR-IRQ-EDGE: The reference testbench reads irq after a write only once write_ok returns, after the response handshake two edges after the write takes effect (axil_timer_tb.v lines 286, 353 and 355), so an irq that follows an IE write or a STATUS clear one or two edges late is not caught. The rise after a count end is timed, under TMR-COUNT-LENGTH.
not_judged.TMR-READY: The reference testbench sees readiness only through the handshakes of the transfers it offers, one at a time: each write and each read runs to its response before the next starts (axil_timer_tb.v lines 96 to 197), and it never reads AWREADY, WREADY or ARREADY otherwise. So the 'only if' halves (no acceptance while a response waits or while the same half is held) and readiness across the two directions are never exercised; a block that drops AWREADY while RVALID is high is not caught. Writes completing in either order are judged under TMR-ORDER.
not_judged.TMR-READ-VALUE: The reference testbench never reads a register on an edge on which that register changes: COUNT only while it holds still (see TMR-COUNT-READ), CTRL and STATUS only on edges on which no count ends, LOAD never during a write. So a read that returns the value after the accepting edge is not caught.
not_judged.TMR-RESET-EDGE: The reference testbench drives aresetn low only at power up, where BVALID, RVALID and the held halves start unknown rather than high, and in the middle of a count with no transfer in progress (axil_timer_tb.v lines 259 to 267, 293 to 295 and 407 to 411), changing it only between rising edges. So it never sees a pending response or a held half write dropped by reset, and does not tell a synchronous reset from an asynchronous one. The manager rule is an assumption on the testbench, which keeps it.
not_judged.TMR-CLEAN: Lint and synthesis are the RTL stage's own before-review checks, not held-out checks.
not_judged.TMR-TB-ALL: The must-fail check holds the flow's testbench to passing on the reference RTL and failing the four committed timer mutants (cited under mutants), and to nothing more: a testbench that leaves any other requirement of sections 2 to 6 unchecked, or times only some counts to the edge, still passes it.
